Visage.et: 17th century, borrowed from French visage (“face”). Early on often pejoratively, to which context it was ultimately restricted.

Visum.et: 18th century as Visa, from French visa, from Latin visa, plural of visum (“something seen”). The form was later relatinised yielding the contemporary singular in -um.

Visagist.et: Borrowed from French visagiste, by surface analysis, Visage + -ist.

Visier.et: 15th century, from Middle French, from Old French visiere. The sense “sight” (late 16th century) under influence of related visieren, anvisieren (“to keep in view, aim at”).

s: visa office (the section of an embassy which handles visa applications)
